headline: Machine learning for ADMET, drug-food and mutation-driven binding prediction
label: Admet Prediction Models And Benchmarks
summary: Recent papers pair graph and kernel deep learning with uncertainty and split-aware evaluation across ADMET, interaction and mutation-effect tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is machine learning for predicting molecular properties and interactions, with growing attention to how models are evaluated. hdADMET combines heterogeneous network embeddings with a kernel-based deep neural network for multitask ADMET prediction, while HyperDFI applies cross-view hypergraph-graph contrastive learning to drug-food interactions. Protein-level work follows a similar pattern: FamGeo-DDG uses ESM-2 and DSSP features with family-split evaluation, MutBindPred adds antisymmetric constraints for mutation-induced binding affinity changes, and BlindDDG recasts stability prediction as direction-of-change classification. The conformal docking preprint adds calibrated 3D uncertainty boxes through dependence-aware intervals. The notable element across these items is the attention to uncertainty quantification and split-aware evaluation alongside new architectures.
